target.title: fix(copilot): clean up polling abort listeners
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where GitHub Copilot device-code OAuth polling would leave abort listeners on a shared `AbortSignal` after each successful sleep. `once: true` only removes the listener when abort fires, so normal multi-round `authorization_pending` polling accumulates closures and can trigger EventTarget listener leak warnings.

## Why This Change Was Made

`abortableSleep` in the Copilot OAuth helper now settles once on either timer resolve or abort: clear the timer, remove the named `onAbort` listener, then resolve/reject. Already-aborted signals reject immediately without registering a listener. Polling intervals and error text are unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** Each successful poll sleep left an abort listener on the login cancel signal.
**After:** Resolve and abort both release the timer/listener; cancel still surfaces as `Login cancelled`.

## Evidence

Branch: `codex/copilot-poll-listener-cleanup` | Base: `upstream/main` | Head: `d506c35a6c87` | Node: v24.18.0 — Windows

### Regression tests

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ GitHub Copilot OAuth abortable polling sleep > does not accumulate abort listeners across authorization_pending rounds
 ✓ GitHub Copilot OAuth abortable polling sleep > removes the abort listener when cancelled during sleep
 ✓ GitHub Copilot OAuth abortable polling sleep > rejects an already-aborted signal without registering a listener
```

### Diff summary

```text
src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts       | settle-once cleanup for abortableSleep
src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.test.ts  | fake-timer polling listener regressions
```

What was not tested: completing a full interactive browser authorization to obtain a live Copilot access token.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Copilot OAuth poll sleeps no longer accumulate abort listeners on a shared cancel signal after normal (non-abort) wakeups; cancellation during polling still rejects with `Login cancelled` and releases listeners.
**Environment tested:** Windows, Node v24.18.0, patched branch `d506c35a6c87`; production `testing.pollForGitHubAccessToken` / `testing.startDeviceFlow` imported from source via `node --import tsx --trace-warnings`.
**Steps run after the patch:**

1. Import production `testing.pollForGitHubAccessToken` from `src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts` and run multi-round `authorization_pending` polling with **real timers** (80 ms interval), sampling `getEventListeners(signal, "abort")` during the run.
2. Abort during an in-flight poll sleep (2 s interval, abort at 30 ms) and assert listener count returns to 0 with `Login cancelled`.
3. Start a **live** `testing.startDeviceFlow("github.com")`, poll with the returned device code until `authorization_pending`, abort during the real interval, and capture warning diagnostics (`--trace-warnings` + `process.on("warning")`).

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx --no-warnings --trace-warnings -e "<import production testing.* from github-copilot.ts>"

{
  "stubbed": {
    "token": "proof-redacted",
    "peak": 1,
    "final": 0
  },
  "cancel": {
    "before": 1,
    "msg": "Login cancelled",
    "final": 0
  },
  "live": {
    "verificationUri": "https://github.com/login/device",
    "userCodeRedacted": "C1**",
    "intervalMs": 5000,
    "abortAfterMs": 5200,
    "peak": 1,
    "final": 0,
    "cancelMessage": "Login cancelled"
  },
  "warnings": [],
  "warningsEmpty": true
}
```

**Observed result:** Across stubbed multi-round polling and a live github.com device-code pending poll, peak active abort listeners never exceeded 1 and final listener count returned to 0 after each successful sleep and after cancel; `--trace-warnings` captured no EventTarget/listener warnings.
**Not tested:** Completing browser authorization to exchange the live device code for a Copilot access token; full `loginGitHubCopilot` UI prompt path.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp inbound media downloads that stall after Baileys returns a stream (headers/start ok, then no further chunks) would block `downloadInboundMedia` forever via `saveMediaStream`'s unbounded `for await`, so inbound dispatch never produces an agent reply for that message.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Wrap the Baileys AsyncIterable with a local per-chunk idle race (production default `30_000` ms), matching Telegram's download idle floor and the LINE channel pattern (open `#86873`, different owner).
- On timeout, reject with `WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError`, call `iterator.return()` so Node Readable streams are destroyed, and silence the losing `next()` to avoid `unhandledRejection`.
- Tests may pass a short `chunkTimeoutMs`; production omits it and uses the 30s floor (proven with fake timers).
- Does **not** change core `saveMediaStream` / `src/media/store.ts` (avoids competing with LINE `#86873`).
- Timeout error class stays module-private (knip unused-export gate).

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled WhatsApp media body could hang inbound handling for that message indefinitely.

**After:** Idle streams fail closed after 30s with a clear timeout error so the monitor loop can continue.

## Evidence

Head: `ea7699ebddd118f371256e25bdf172add2061953`

Executable negative control + fix proof:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.node.test.ts -- --run -t "chunk-idle|negative" --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[whatsapp media idle negative control] outcome=still-pending wait_ms=150 without_idle_wrap=true
[whatsapp media idle proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=53 chunkTimeoutMs=50 production_ms=30000
[whatsapp media idle proof] production_default_ms=30000 timed_out=true
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed | 11 skipped (16)
```

- **Negative control (executable):** same never-yielding AsyncIterable consumed with bare `for await` (no idle wrap) stays `still-pending` after 150ms — proves the pre-fix hang fixture.
- **After fix:** `downloadInboundMedia` with `chunkTimeoutMs: 50` rejects in ~53ms; production default advances fake timers to 30s and rejects with `chunkTimeoutMs: 30000`; `iterator.return()` called once on timeout.
- Touched: `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.ts` (+ colocated test). Sibling LINE/Telegram idle floors unchanged (different owners).

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(usage): ignore invalid Z.ai reset timestamps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Z.ai usage fetch converts `nextResetTime` with `new Date(...).getTime()`. Invalid strings produce `NaN`, which is then stored on the usage window as `resetAt` and can poison downstream reset/cooldown logic that expects a finite timestamp or an unset value.

This is provider-contract hardening at the Z.ai usage parser boundary: untrusted quota metadata must not introduce non-finite numbers into domain objects.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.zai.ts`, keep `resetAt` only when `Number.isFinite(parsedReset)` so invalid reset strings are ignored while valid ISO timestamps still populate `resetAt`.

## User Impact

**Before:** Invalid `nextResetTime` values could yield `resetAt: NaN` on Z.ai usage windows.
**After:** Invalid reset strings leave `resetAt` undefined; valid ISO resets still work.

## Evidence

Branch: `codex/zai-invalid-reset-time` | Base: `upstream/main` | Head: `ed45a4bf` | Node: v24.18.0 — Windows

### Diff summary

```text
src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.zai.ts       | finite reset guard on parsed nextResetTime
src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.zai.test.ts  | invalid + valid ISO reset regression
```

What was not tested: a live upstream quota payload that actually contains an invalid `nextResetTime` string (this account returns a coding-plan error with empty windows).

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Invalid truthy `nextResetTime` no longer becomes `resetAt: NaN` on Z.ai usage windows; valid ISO resets still populate finite `resetAt`. The same production `fetchZaiUsage` path is used for live authenticated calls and parser hardening checks.
**Environment tested:** Windows, Node v24.18.0, patched branch `ed45a4bf`; production `fetchZaiUsage` imported from `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.zai.ts` via `node --import tsx` (script: `zai-invalid-reset-proof.mts`).
**Steps run after the patch:**

1. Run `node --import tsx --no-warnings zai-invalid-reset-proof.mts` against production `fetchZaiUsage`.
2. With `ZAI_API_KEY` set (not logged), call the live `https://api.z.ai/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit` endpoint through the same production function.
3. On the same production function, feed a synthetic 200 JSON body containing `nextResetTime: "not-a-date"` plus a valid ISO monthly reset and inspect parsed windows.

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx --no-warnings zai-invalid-reset-proof.mts

zai-invalid-reset-proof start
live fetchZaiUsage:
{
  "provider": "zai",
  "displayName": "z.ai",
  "error": "current user does not have a coding plan",
  "windowCount": 0,
  "windows": []
}
parser control: nextResetTime="not-a-date" -> getTime=NaN Number.isNaN=true
production fetchZaiUsage invalid+valid payload: {
  "windows": [
    {
      "label": "Tokens (6h)",
      "usedPercent": 32,
      "resetAtIsFinite": false
    },
    {
      "label": "Monthly",
      "usedPercent": 12.5,
      "resetAt": 1767830400000,
      "resetAtIsFinite": true
    }
  ]
}
{
  "livePathOk": true,
  "invalidResetDropped": true,
  "validResetFinite": true,
  "noNaN": true
}
```

**Observed result:** Live Z.ai accepted the API key and returned a structured usage error through production `fetchZaiUsage` (empty windows because this account has no coding plan). On the same production parser path, invalid `nextResetTime` is dropped (`resetAt` omitted) while the valid ISO monthly reset remains a finite epoch milliseconds value; summary reports `noNaN: true`.
**Not tested:** A live quota payload that actually contains an invalid `nextResetTime` string. This account returns the coding-plan missing error with empty windows, so incidence of malformed upstream reset strings remains unverified; the change is parser-boundary hardening plus live path smoke.

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)
- focused Slack replies + identity-fallback tests passed (85 tests)
- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. Callable public SDK budget was raised with the additive predicate.

target.title: fix(cli-backends): surface config-defined custom CLI backends in runtime model bindings (fixes #106373)
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `sessions.compact` throws `MissingAgentHarnessError` for sessions running on a config-defined custom CLI backend — a backend declared only under `agents.defaults.cliBackends`, not owned by any plugin. Execution of the same session works correctly because `resolveCliBackendConfig` recognizes config-only backends, but the compaction and harness-selection paths do not, because `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` only consults the plugin runtime registry and optional setup registry — never the user's `agents.defaults.cliBackends` config.

Concrete example: defining a second Claude Code account (`claude-cli-max`) with a different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` under `cliBackends` works for agent turns, but every `sessions.compact` request against that session fails with `MissingAgentHarnessError: Requested agent harness "claude-cli-max" is not registered.`

## Why This Change Was Made

`listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` now also surfaces config-defined custom CLI backends that resolve to a valid config (non-null `resolveCliBackendConfig`). This aligns it with the existing `isCliProvider` function in `model-selection-cli.ts`, which already recognizes config-only backends. The asymmetry — `isCliProvider` sees the backend but `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` and its callers (`isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider`, `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding`, `resolveCliRuntimeCanonicalProvider`) do not — caused the compaction and harness precheck paths to miss config-only backends while the execution path handled them.

Two additional pass-through fixes: `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding` and `resolveCliRuntimeCanonicalProvider` now forward `config`/`env` to `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` instead of calling it without parameters. A single call site in `harness/selection.ts` now forwards `cfg` to `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider` (the other call site in the same file already did).

Backends already in the plugin registry are never duplicated; backends without a valid `command` are silently omitted.

## User Impact

Users with config-defined custom CLI backends (e.g. multiple Claude Code accounts, or any non-plugin CLI runtime) can now run `sessions.compact` without `MissingAgentHarnessError`. Agent execution, harness selection, and compaction preflight all treat these backends consistently.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/cli-backends.ts` — the three-line core change adding config-only backends to `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings`, plus two config-forwarding fixes.
- `src/agents/harness/selection.ts` — one-line forwarding of `cfg` to `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider`.
- Regression tests in `src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts` — six new cases covering: inclusion of a valid config-only backend, resolution via `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding`, `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider` returning true, omission when no config is passed or the backend lacks a command, and non-duplication of plugin-registered backends with config-level overrides.
- Full test run: `pnpm test src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts` — 64 passed; `pnpm test src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.test.ts src/agents/model-selection-cli.test.ts` — 25 passed. No regressions.

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts -t "config-defined backends"

 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > includes a config-only custom CLI backend with a valid command
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > resolves a binding for a config-only backend via resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider returns true for a config-only backend
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > omits a config-only backend when no config is passed
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > omits a config-only backend with no command
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > does not duplicate a plugin-registered backend with a config-level override

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

The six tests exercise `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` (before — no config → custom backend absent), `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding` (after — with config → custom backend bound), and `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider` (after — returns true), covering all three patched functions plus the edge cases.

target.title: Fix/OpenAI device code request timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running OpenAI Codex device-code login (`openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code`, or the equivalent configure/wizard auth choice) could hang forever when a single `auth.openai.com` HTTP request stopped responding.

Before this patch, the flow enforced a 15-minute poll-loop deadline around authorization waiting, and callers could cancel via `AbortSignal`, but the three HTTP calls for user-code request, authorization poll, and token exchange had no per-request operation deadline covering both headers and body reads. A stalled TCP/proxy/blackhole response, or a server that returned headers and then stalled the body, could leave the CLI spinner stuck.

## Why This Change Was Made

Treat each device-code HTTP call as one timed operation: headers fetch plus bounded body read under `buildOAuthRequestSignal` (caller `AbortSignal` composed with `AbortSignal.timeout`, 30s, aligned with the sibling ChatGPT browser OAuth token request timeout). Poll requests clamp that timeout to the remaining 15-minute authorization deadline and retry only on operation timeout (including post-header body stalls) until the overall deadline expires. Caller cancel (Ctrl-C / wizard abort) remains distinguishable and does not retry. User-code and token-exchange timeouts fail fast with a clear error.

Body/fetch aborts rethrow the composed signal reason so undici `AbortError` collapse does not erase `TimeoutError` vs caller cancel distinguishability.

Scope stays OpenAI Codex device-code login HTTP only; browser OAuth and other providers are unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung device-code HTTP request (or a post-header body stall) could block `models auth login --device-code` indefinitely, even past the advertised 15-minute authorization window, while still depending on the overall poll deadline for happy-path waiting.

**After:** Each device-code request+body read aborts after 30 seconds (or sooner near the overall deadline). Poll timeouts retry within the 15-minute window; caller cancel aborts immediately without retry; user-code and token-exchange stalls surface an explicit timeout error instead of hanging forever.

## Evidence

- `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.ts` — `buildOAuthRequestSignal` composes caller cancel + 30s operation deadline across fetch + body read; poll retries only on operation timeout
- Regression: `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts`
  - hung user-code / token-exchange abort with timeout error
  - poll retries after `TimeoutError` and completes
  - caller cancel during hung fetch / poll wait / post-header body stall does not retry or map to timeout
  - real `node:http` partial-body stall coverage
  - success path asserts fetches carry an `AbortSignal`

### Unit regression

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text

 ✓ aborts an in-flight hung user-code request on caller cancel 1ms
 ✓ aborts hung user-code requests instead of waiting forever 0ms
 ✓ retries device authorization polls after a per-request timeout 0ms
 ✓ does not retry authorization polls after caller cancel 0ms
 ✓ aborts hung token exchange requests instead of waiting forever 0ms
 ✓ aborts when user-code headers arrive but the body never completes 130ms
 ✓ cancels a post-header body stall on caller abort without mapping to timeout 37ms
 ✓ retries authorization polls after a post-header body stall 123ms
 ✓ aborts when token-exchange headers arrive but the body never completes 124ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
 Duration  4.01s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 14.04s
```

### Standalone runtime proof (outside Vitest)

```bash
node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-openai-device-code-proof/standalone.mts
```

target.title: fix(line): cap user profile cache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an unbounded in-process `userProfileCache` in the LINE send path (`extensions/line/src/send.ts`). Profile lookups are cached for 5 minutes (TTL) but had no entry-count cap, so gateways serving many distinct LINE users accumulate Map entries indefinitely until process restart.

**Concrete scenario:** A LINE gateway processing inbound messages from 10 000 distinct users over several hours caches each `getUserProfile` result. With no size cap, the cache grows without bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a 1 024-entry cap via the existing `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`, matching Slack / Discord / Nextcloud Talk channel caches.

`touchLineUserProfileCache` deletes + sets so Map insertion order refreshes on both write and TTL-valid read hits (same LRU-on-access pattern as `extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts`). Active users stay under the cap; idle oldest-inserted entries evict first.

No config/env knobs. TTL behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** Long-lived LINE gateways accumulate one `userProfileCache` entry per distinct user indefinitely.

**After:** Cache stays at ≤ 1 024 entries. Recently touched profiles survive eviction; untouched oldest entries are pruned. First 1 024 distinct users behave as before until the cap is exceeded.

## Evidence

- `extensions/line/src/send.ts` — `LINE_USER_PROFILE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 1024`, `touchLineUserProfileCache` (delete + set + `pruneMapToMaxSize`) on write and TTL hit
- `extensions/line/src/monitor.ts` — inbound path calls `getUserDisplayName` → `getUserProfile`
- Sibling pattern: `extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts` (`getCachedSlackConversationInfo` / `setCachedSlackConversationInfo`)
- Shared helper: `src/infra/map-size.ts` via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime` (`pruneMapToMaxSize`)
- Regression: `extensions/line/src/send.test.ts`
  - eviction past cap via `getUserDisplayName`
  - recently touched entry retained under cap

### Caller-path Vitest

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/send.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text

 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/send.test.ts > LINE send helpers > evicts oldest profile cache entries once the cache exceeds its cap 8ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/send.test.ts > LINE send helpers > keeps recently touched profile entries under the cache cap 9ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 8.64s
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** LINE user-profile Map no longer grows without bound; active entries refresh insertion order so they survive pruning.
- **Canonical reachability path:**

```text
LINE inbound webhook (monitor)
  → getUserDisplayName(userId)
  → getUserProfile(userId)
  → touchLineUserProfileCache (delete + set)

```

Only `@line/bot-sdk` `MessagingApiClient.getProfile` is stubbed (no live LINE credentials in this environment). There is no DI seam for the Messaging API client; production constructs `new messagingApi.MessagingApiClient(...)` inside `createLineMessagingClient`.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Cap and LRU-on-access match Slack conversation-info and other channel `pruneMapToMaxSize` caches. No new config/env surface.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/send.test.ts --reporter=verbose

# only MessagingApiClient.getProfile stubbed via Node module loader):
OPENCLAW_ROOT=/tmp/openclaw-pr-fixes/101741 \
  node --import tsx \
  --import /tmp/line-user-profile-cache-proof/register-line-bot-sdk-stub.mjs \
  /tmp/line-user-profile-cache-proof/line-user-profile-cache-proof.mts
```



Regression flow (caller path `getUserDisplayName`):

1. Resolve `U-first` → 1 API call, cached
2. Resolve `U-fill-1` … `U-fill-1024` → 1 024 more API calls; `U-first` evicted at cap

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox exec-server subprocesses (both the process RPC path and the streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream `error` events, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox child process exits or its pipes break, the Node stream layer emits `error` on the child's stdout/stderr `Readable` streams. With no `error` listener attached, Node re-throws the event, which bubbles into a process-fatal unhandled error and terminates the exec-server bridge. Both subprocess owners — `processes.ts` (process RPC) and `http.ts` (streaming HTTP) — had this gap.

The fix attaches a no-op `error` listener on `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` at each spawn point, mirroring the repo-standard pattern already used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`. The process `close` handler stays authoritative for lifecycle and finalization.

Rebased onto current `main`; resolved a conflict with #103617 (defer sandbox cleanup until process close), which restructured both spawn sites into a `try/catch`. The no-op listeners are now attached after the guarded spawn, preserving that ownership.

## User Impact

The Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess output pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**Production change (both subprocess owners):** after the guarded `spawn`, before the `data` listeners, each spawn site attaches no-op `error` listeners on `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` (`processes.ts`, `http.ts`), mirroring `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`. The `close` handler stays authoritative for lifecycle/finalization.

**Real integration proof — executes the patched code outside Vitest over a real WebSocket bridge.** A standalone `tsx` harness imports and calls the real exported entry points — `startProcess()` → `runProcess()` (process-RPC owner) and `httpRequest({streamResponse:true})` → `runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest()` (HTTP owner) — over a real `ws` bridge. Only the sandbox backend seam is stubbed; the `spawn`, stdout/stderr listeners, close lifecycle, JSON-RPC notifications, and ws bridge are all real. No `spawn` module mock, no Vitest.

Process-RPC owner — real `runProcess`, real streaming child, induced real stdout/stderr pipe error; the bridge survives and stays usable:

```text
[host] real bridge streamed 10 process/output notifications over the ws
[host] inducing a real stdout/stderr pipe error on the real child ...
[host] bridge still usable after error: readProcess ok (chunks=10, exited=true)
[host] ws bridge socket.readyState = 1 (1=OPEN)
[host] child close after the error emitted process/closed = true
[host] PASS: real patched runProcess survived the induced pipe error; bridge stayed OPEN
```

Negative control on the same real path — removing the fix's real stdout error listener from the live child reproduces the pre-fix crash, proving the listener is load-bearing:

```text
[host] stripped the fix's real stdout error listener (pre-fix state)
[host] inducing a real stdout/stderr pipe error on the real child ...
[host] UNCAUGHT EPIPE: induced sandbox stdout pipe failure -> exec-server bridge host crashed
[shell] exit=1
```

HTTP owner — real `runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest` executes end-to-end with the same guards attached:

```text
[host] real httpRequest(streaming) executed end-to-end: status=200, bodyDeltas=1
[host] ws bridge socket.readyState = 1 (1=OPEN)
[host] PASS: real patched runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest executed over the real bridge with the stdout/stderr guards attached
```

<details>
<summary>Proof integration harness (executes the real exec-server entry points; backend seam stubbed, spawn/streams/bridge real)</summary>

```ts
import { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from "ws";
import { startProcess, readProcess, terminateProcess } from "./sandbox-exec-server/processes.js";
import { httpRequest } from "./sandbox-exec-server/http.js";

let hostCrashed = false;
process.on("uncaughtException", (e) => {
  hostCrashed = true;
  console.log(`[host] UNCAUGHT ${e.message} -> exec-server bridge host crashed`);
  process.exit(1);
});

async function socketPair() {
  const wss = new WebSocketServer({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: 0 });
  await new Promise((r) => wss.once("listening", r));
  const client = new WebSocket(`ws://127.0.0.1:${wss.address().port}`);
  const server = await new Promise((res) => wss.once("connection", res));
  await new Promise((r) => client.once("open", r));
  return { wss, client, server };
}

// Stub ONLY the backend seam; buildExecSpec spawns a REAL child.
const makeExecServer = (argv) => ({
  sandbox: {
    containerWorkdir: "/tmp",
    backend: {
      buildExecSpec: async () => ({ argv, env: process.env, finalizeToken: "tok" }),
      finalizeExec: async () => {},
    },
  },
});

// mode "process-survive": run real startProcess, induce a real stdout/stderr error, assert bridge OPEN.
// mode "process-strip":   same, but managed.child.stdout.removeAllListeners("error") first -> host crashes.
// mode "http-execute":    run real httpRequest({streamResponse:true}) end-to-end over the real ws bridge.
// (full runnable harness kept in the contributor outputs)
```

</details>

**Mutation-sensitive regression test** (`sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts`): captures the real spawned child and emits `error` on the real `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` for both the process RPC and streaming HTTP paths, asserting each stream carries an `error` listener, that emitting the error does not throw, that the WebSocket bridge stays `OPEN`, and (process path) that the bridge still runs follow-up work. Removing either production listener makes the test fail.

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

The same no-op `error` listener pattern already ships in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`, confirming this is the repo-standard approach.

```text
$ cd /tmp/openclaw-proof-101777 && cat stream-error-lifecycle.txt

=== proof: http stream-error lifecycle ===

  ws connected, readyState=1
  http/request sent (child alive, no headers)
  child pid=2714157 alive=true
  stdout EPIPE emitted
  request rejected: sandbox http/request output stream error: EPIPE: broken pipe
  ws readyState=1
  finalizeExec calls before close: 0
  finalizeExec: {"status":"failed","exitCode":1,"timedOut":false}
  finalizeExec calls after close: 1

=== summary ===
  settled               = YES
  ws survived            = YES
  no finalize before close = YES
  finalize after close   = YES
```

The induced stream-error proof confirms: (1) request settles with error before headers, (2) WebSocket bridge stays OPEN, (3) finalizeExec is NOT called before child close — the lease is held for the full process lifetime, and (4) finalizeExec is called exactly once after close with status=failed.

**ClawSweeper P1 repair:** the streaming HTTP stdout/stderr error path now settles the request once, sends `SIGTERM` to the one-shot helper, and still leaves backend `finalizeExec` owned by the child `close` handler. The regression child intentionally ignores `SIGTERM`, which proves the request is settled and termination is requested while `finalizeExec` remains at zero until the child is force-closed; after close, `finalizeExec` is called exactly once with `status: "failed"`.

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Zalo `resolveZaloProxyFetch` retained one `makeProxyFetch` entry per distinct proxy URL in a process-lifetime `Map` with no eviction. Config churn or high-cardinality proxy URLs could therefore grow gateway memory without a hard bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Cap `proxyCache` at 64 entries using the shared `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper after every successful insert (same pattern as Nextcloud Talk room cache / MS Teams team-group cache / Mattermost opaque-target cache).
- Insertion-order eviction keeps newest proxy fetchers; cache-hit identity and empty-URL behavior are unchanged.
- Adds a focused regression that fills `max+1` distinct URLs, proves the oldest entry is rebuilt on next use, and confirms a mid-window entry still hits.

No new config/env surface. Does not change Bot API timeouts (`#104017`) or other Zalo send paths.

## User Impact

**Before:** Long-running Zalo gateways could retain an unbounded number of proxy fetcher closures as distinct proxy URLs appeared.

**After:** At most 64 distinct proxy fetchers are retained; older ones are dropped and rebuilt on next use.

target.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Codex app-server over `websocket`/`unix` transport would hang forever on `initialize`/RPC when a peer accepted TCP but never completed the WebSocket upgrade. Pending frames never flush and the client never sees a transport exit, so the run cannot fail closed or reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a private `buildCodexAppServerWebSocketOptions` that sets `handshakeTimeout: 30_000` (same floor as Slack relay / Mattermost / Discord gateway).
- Both TCP and Unix upgrade paths consume that builder.
- Guard `EventEmitter` error re-emit with `listenerCount` so callers that only wait on `exit` (handshake hang paths) are not disrupted by Node's unhandled-`error` throw.
- Regressions observe production wiring in source (knip-safe) and prove stalled-handshake exit + `initialize` failure with a short test-only hang floor.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Codex app-server endpoint that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin `initialize`/RPC forever on that attempt.

**After:** Handshake waits fail closed after 30s (`Opening handshake has timed out` → transport `exit` / client error), so the run can stop or recover instead of hanging.

## Evidence

Compete check (live, before push): no open PR for `createWebSocketTransport` / Codex app-server `handshakeTimeout` (siblings Mattermost `#105553`, Signal `#106471`, ClickClack `#106485`, QQBot `#106484` are different owners).

Head: `ca0c6dbdc9b2adcf44cce506eaf2566a409f1e7c`

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts --reporter=verbose

✓ uses a 30s handshakeTimeout matching Slack relay / Mattermost
[codex handshake proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=201 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=200 production_ms=30000
✓ emits exit when the websocket handshake never completes
[codex handshake initialize proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=201 message=initialize transport failed after request write: Opening handshake has timed out
✓ fails initialize when the websocket handshake never completes
```

target.title: fix(plugins): allow user-installed and generated plugins to use api.runtime.state
target.body:
## Summary
- The \`state\` proxy in \`src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts\` only trusted plugins with \`origin === "bundled"\` or \`trustedOfficialInstall === true\`.
- Plugins installed by the user (global/workspace origins) — including plugins generated locally via OpenClaw's plugin-generation flow — were blocked from \`api.runtime.state\` (openKeyedStore / openSyncKeyedStore / openChannelIngressQueue).
- This caused \`register()\` to crash for such plugins (observed as \`api.runtime.state is undefined\` on \`2026.7.1-beta.5\`, and a thrown "only available for trusted plugins in this release." on newer builds).
- Extend the trust gate to also allow \`global\` and \`workspace\` origins. \`state\` is namespaced per-plugin persistent storage, so this is safe for the user's own explicitly-installed code.

## Root cause
\`assertPluginStateAllowed()\` in the \`state\` getter rejected any plugin whose record was neither \`bundled\` nor a trusted official install. A locally-generated \`@openclaw/codex\` plugin (origin \`global\`, installed under \`~/.openclaw/npm/projects/...\`) hit this and crashed on register.

## Test plan
- Added \`src/plugins/registry-runtime-state-gate.test.ts\` asserting that \`api.runtime.state.openSyncKeyedStore(...)\` does not throw for \`global\`, \`workspace\`, \`bundled\`, and trusted-official origins.
- All 4 new tests pass; neighboring \`registry.runtime-config.test.ts\` still passes.

## Notes for review
- This broadens the trust boundary to all user-installed plugins. \`openKeyedStore\`/\`openSyncKeyedStore\` are per-plugin-namespaced, so the blast radius is the plugin's own state. If maintainers prefer a narrower gate (e.g. only plugins generated by OpenClaw, or a separate \`userTrusted\` flag), I can adjust.
- Affects \`2026.7.1-beta.5\` and later; a backport to the \`2026.7.1\` release line may be warranted.

Closes #103668

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running bash commands through agents could see ANSI/OSC control-sequence fragments leak into streamed tool output, final bash results, and full-output spill files when a process split a terminal sequence across output callbacks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix adds a reusable incremental ANSI sequence stripper in terminal-core and lets the bash output accumulator use one sanitizer instance for the lifetime of each command. This preserves streaming and bounded-memory behavior while keeping one-shot `stripAnsiSequences()` semantics unchanged for existing callers.

## User Impact

Bash output sanitization is now invariant to callback chunking for OSC and CSI sequences. Agents and users receive the same clean output whether the process emits a complete sequence in one callback or splits it across callbacks.

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two operator visibility gaps in OpenClaw security posture checks:

1. **`plugins.load.paths` trust-boundary risk** — Operators can point `plugins.load.paths` at arbitrary local directories, but `openclaw security audit` did not evaluate those configured paths for filesystem risk (world-writable paths, missing entries, bundled aliases, synced folders) before runtime plugin load.
2. **SecretRef env fallback visibility** — Runtime secret resolution can fall back to environment variables in some configurations; operators lacked a dedicated audit finding when that fallback was active.

**Concrete example:** An operator adds a world-writable `/tmp/demo-plugin` to `plugins.load.paths` and configures gateway auth via SecretRef that silently resolves from `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`. Before this PR, `openclaw security audit` did not surface either risk explicitly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `collectPluginLoadPathFindings` and wires SecretRef env-fallback diagnostics into `openclaw security audit` / doctor health contributions so misconfiguration surfaces as explicit findings instead of silent trust expansion.

Shared diagnostics live in `src/secrets/secretref-env-fallback-diagnostics.ts` so audit and doctor use one detector. `isActiveGatewayTokenSurface` forwards caller-provided `env` into `resolveGatewayAuth` so injected audit/doctor env is not ignored.

## User Impact

**Before:** Risky plugin load paths and active SecretRef env fallbacks could go unnoticed.

**After:** `openclaw security audit` emits `plugins.load_paths.*` and `secrets.ref_env_fallback_used` findings operators can act on. Doctor lint exposes the same SecretRef fallback via `core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback`. No runtime behavior change unless operators remediate.

## Evidence

- `src/security/audit-plugin-load-paths.ts` — `collectPluginLoadPathFindings`
- `src/security/audit-secretref-env-fallback.ts` — maps shared diagnostics to audit findings
- `src/secrets/secretref-env-fallback-diagnostics.ts` — shared diagnostic collector
- `src/flows/doctor-core-checks.ts` — `core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback`
- `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts` — wired into `doctor:gateway-auth`; `doctor:default-account-routing` preserved
- `docs/gateway/security/audit-checks.md` — catalog rows for the new check IDs

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `openclaw security audit` and `openclaw doctor --lint` now emit the new warnings for a real risky config (world-writable `plugins.load.paths` + unresolved gateway SecretRef falling back to `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`).

target.title: feat(cron): serve cron run history from the task ledger
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

One cron execution today produces three overlapping records: a rich `cron_run_logs` row, a deliberately thin `task_runs` mirror (silent, `not_applicable`, best-effort), and a session-registry row — plus dual-written `CronJobState` last-run fields. Downstream, task maintenance needs a cron-specific recovery branch that cross-reads two cron stores, and the Control UI shows the same execution twice at different fidelity (Automations run history vs Tasks page).

Part 1 of 2 for #106041: make the task ledger the authoritative record for cron executions and flip the external read paths, while keeping the legacy `cron_run_logs` dual-write as a revert safety net. PR 2 migrates old history, deletes the run-log stack, and unifies cancellation.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `task_runs` gains a generic nullable `detail_json` column (additive `ensureColumn` migration + regenerated Kysely types). Cron owns the codec ([task-run-detail.ts](../blob/HEAD/src/cron/task-run-detail.ts)) between run outcomes, ledger detail, and the **unchanged** `CronRunLogEntry` wire shape.
- Cron writes full-fidelity terminal rows (status vocabulary, delivery trace, `errorReason`, `triggerFired`, `nextRunAtMs`, model/usage) instead of the lobotomized mirror; skipped runs now create immediately-terminal rows so history parity holds.
- `cron.runs` RPC, the CLI run-history poll, and task-maintenance cron recovery read from the ledger ([task-run-history.ts](../blob/HEAD/src/cron/task-run-history.ts)); the maintenance cron branch shrinks from two cross-store readers to a ledger self-lookup, and `configureTaskRegistryMaintenance` loses its `cronStorePath` parameter.
- Startup crash recovery improves: a run that finished before the crash is restored from its finalized ledger row (with `record-only` failure-alert cooldown restore) instead of being reported as "interrupted".
- Same-millisecond executions get distinct ledger rows via a run-id discriminator; the reservation timestamp keys recovery.

- Existing history migrates automatically: a one-shot state migration ([state-migrations.cron-run-logs.ts](../blob/HEAD/src/infra/state-migrations.cron-run-logs.ts)) imports `cron_run_logs` rows into the ledger at first DB open — no manual doctor step — with deterministic import ids for idempotency and dual-write-aware duplicate matching.
- History reads stay scoped to the configured cron store: `cron_run_logs` partitions by `store_key`, so ledger detail records the store key and `readCronTaskRunHistoryPage` filters by it (kept out of the wire shape; test-locked).

Non-goals here (PR 2): stopping the dual-write, dropping `cron_run_logs` + `cron.runLog.*` config keys, per-source retention, cancel unification. No protocol schema, UI, or config changes; `CronRunLogEntrySchema` consumers (Control UI, macOS, Android) see identical responses.

## User Impact

No visible behavior change. Cron run history is served from the shared task ledger; Automations history and the Tasks page now describe the same rows. Crash-interrupted-but-completed runs report their true outcome after restart instead of a synthetic interruption error.

## Evidence

- Parity tests: ledger-served history equals legacy run-log responses across ok/error/timeout/skipped, delivery statuses, trigger, telemetry, paging, and text-query filtering (`src/cron/task-run-history.test.ts`).
- Race matrix: operator-cancel precedence, lost-row overwrite, same-ms collisions, skip rows (`src/cron/service/task-runs.test.ts`, `ops.test.ts`, `timer.test.ts`).
- Serialized-detail shape locked behind the indexed LIKE prefixes so codec field reordering fails loudly.
- **Production-data migration proof**: against a copied 247 MB production state DB (2,750 legacy run-log rows, 5 jobs, 952 pre-upgrade task rows): 2,750/2,750 imported, 0 malformed, ledger vs legacy reader totals equal and first page byte-identical, second open idempotent (no double import).
- Focused packs green locally (~1,750 tests across cron/tasks/gateway/infra surfaces); structured second-model review run to zero accepted findings (two accepted findings fixed: legacy runId recovery, store-key scoping + auto-migration); full gates on hosted CI/Testbox.

target.title: fix(skills): globally-installed ClawHub skills falsely show as not tracked [AI-assisted]
target.body:
> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

Closes #105530

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who install a ClawHub skill **globally** (`openclaw skills install <slug> --global`, living under the managed dir `~/.openclaw/skills/<slug>` and tracked in the **global** lockfile `~/.openclaw/.clawhub/lock.json`) would see the skill falsely reported as `ClawHub link invalid` in `openclaw skills status` and the Control UI, with the message:

> Skill `<slug>` has ClawHub origin metadata but is not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile.

The skill is in fact correctly installed and tracked - just in the global lockfile, not the workspace one.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` read the ClawHub lockfile exclusively from the workspace directory (`readClawHubSkillsLockfileStatusSync(workspaceDir)`) and passed that single read to `resolveClawHubSkillStatusLinkSync` for every non-bundled skill. For a globally-installed skill (`source: "openclaw-managed"`), the tracking entry lives in the **managed** lockfile at `<dirname(managedSkillsDir)>/.clawhub/lock.json`, so the workspace lookup misses it and returns `invalid`.

The fix resolves the link status for `openclaw-managed` skills against the managed lockfile (and the managed parent dir, so the expected-install-dir check matches the skill dir) instead of the workspace lockfile. Workspace-local skills are unchanged. Detection uses the loader-assigned `source` rather than a lexical path check, because managed skill roots may contain symlinks whose resolved `baseDir` sits outside the `managedSkillsDir` tree.

## User Impact

Globally installed ClawHub skills now show as correctly `linked` in `openclaw skills status` and the Control UI skills view, instead of a false `ClawHub link invalid` / "not tracked" warning. Workspace-local skill status is unaffected.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof captured on Windows 10 by running the production `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` against real on-disk lockfiles (standalone `tsx` repro script run locally; before/after output below). The script creates a managed (global) install - skill dir under `managedSkillsDir` with `.clawhub/origin.json`, plus a global lockfile at `<managedParent>/.clawhub/lock.json` tracking it - and a separate workspace whose own lockfile does **not** track the skill.

BEFORE (unpatched main) - the globally-installed skill is falsely `invalid`, read against the **workspace** lockfile:

```
"skillSource": "openclaw-managed",
"clawhub": {
  "status": "invalid",
  "valid": false,
  "reason": "Skill \"agentreceipt\" has ClawHub origin metadata but is not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile.",
  "slug": "agentreceipt",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-workspace-fYctHw\\.clawhub\\lock.json"
}
```

AFTER (this patch) - the same skill is correctly `linked`, read against the **managed (global)** lockfile:

```
"skillSource": "openclaw-managed",
"clawhub": {
  "status": "linked",
  "valid": true,
  "registry": "https://clawhub.ai",
  "slug": "agentreceipt",
  "installedVersion": "1.2.3",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-managed-83CHpB\\.clawhub\\lock.json"
}
```

Regression tests added in `src/skills/discovery/status.test.ts`:
- links a globally-installed skill via the managed lockfile (asserts `status: "linked"`)
- reports a globally-installed skill as `invalid` when it is absent from the managed lockfile (guards against falsely linking)

Full skill-status suite passes (`pnpm test -- src/skills/discovery/status.test.ts` -> 13 passed, 1 skipped on win32).

## Real Behavior Proof

- Behavior addressed: Globally installed ClawHub skills (`source: "openclaw-managed"`) are falsely reported as `invalid` / "not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile" because `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` only consults the workspace lockfile.
- Real environment tested: Windows 10, Node v22.22.3, OpenClaw main @ 50e5ffcd25, running the production `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` function from `src/skills/discovery/status.ts` via `pnpm exec tsx`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: a standalone `tsx` script builds a managed/global install (skill dir + `.clawhub/origin.json` + global lockfile tracking the slug) and a separate workspace whose lockfile omits the slug, then calls `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus(workspaceDir, { managedSkillsDir, entries })` and prints the resolved `clawhub` status.
- Evidence after fix:
```
AFTER (patched):
"clawhub": { "status": "linked", "valid": true, "slug": "agentreceipt",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-managed-83CHpB\\.clawhub\\lock.json" }

BEFORE (unpatched main):
"clawhub": { "status": "invalid", "valid": false,
  "reason": "Skill \"agentreceipt\" has ClawHub origin metadata but is not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile.",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-workspace-fYctHw\\.clawhub\\lock.json" }
```
- Observed result after fix: The globally-installed skill resolves to `status: "linked"` against the managed (global) lockfile instead of `invalid` against the workspace lockfile. The `lockPath` in the resolved status now points at the global lockfile.
- What was not tested: End-to-end through a running gateway / live Control UI render; the real `openclaw skills status` CLI against a real `~/.openclaw` home. The proof exercises the real production status function with real on-disk lockfiles, which is the exact code path the CLI and UI consume.

## Human Verification

Verified: the production `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` code path with real on-disk managed + workspace lockfiles (before/after), scoped `pnpm test` for the skills status suite, `pnpm tsgo` (type check), `pnpm format:check`, scoped `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files. Not verified: Swift (skipped on Windows), full `pnpm test` suite, live Control UI rendering. Note: local `pnpm build` (tsdown) hit a V8 out-of-memory crash on this Windows machine (a known low-memory local-env quirk, unrelated to this 3-line logic change); relying on CI's build check on a properly-sized runner.

## Security Impact

- Does this change authentication, authorization, or trust boundaries? No.
- Does this change credential, secret, or token handling? No.
- Does this change sandboxing or process isolation? No.
- Does this change network boundaries or external API calls? No.
- Does this introduce a new trust boundary or change an existing one? No.

No CODEOWNERS secops paths are touched (`src/skills/` is not secops-owned). The change only affects which local lockfile is consulted for a status display.

## Compatibility / Migration

No config, API, CLI, or lockfile-format changes. The set of inputs/outputs of `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` is unchanged; only the accuracy of the `clawhub` status for globally-installed skills improves. No migration required.

## Failure Recovery

If the managed lockfile read regresses, globally-installed skills would revert to the prior `invalid` / "not tracked" display behavior - a cosmetic status misreport, not a crash or data loss. The change is read-only with respect to lockfiles (no writes), so there is no risk of lockfile corruption. Reverting the commit fully restores prior behavior.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk**: A skill whose loader-assigned `source` is `openclaw-managed` but whose lockfile entry legitimately lives in the workspace lockfile would now be looked up in the managed lockfile. **Mitigation**: managed skills are, by definition, installed under `managedSkillsDir` and tracked in the managed lockfile; workspace-local skills use other `source` values and are unaffected. Added a regression test for the "absent from managed lockfile" case to ensure such a skill still reports `invalid` rather than falsely `linked`.
- **Risk**: Competing/sibling PR on the same issue. **Mitigation**: this PR supplies the real-behavior-proof (real production-function output with real on-disk lockfiles, before/after) that the issue's proof gate requires, rather than a screenshot.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I understand review conversations belong to the reviewer and I should not resolve them myself unless requested.

target.title: fix(tlon): clear SSE connect timeout after failed openStream
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon Urbit SSE `openStream` armed a 60s connect `setTimeout` and only cleared it after a successful `urbitFetch`. When the connect fetch rejected (DNS/SSRF/network) or returned non-OK, the timer stayed armed until it fired, and reconnect storms could stack dangling timers in the Gateway process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the connect fetch in `try/finally` and always `clearTimeout`, matching the zalouser probe timeout cleanup pattern, so failed connects release the timer immediately without changing the connect deadline or stream lifecycle.

## User Impact

Flaky Urbit hosts no longer leave dangling connect timers in long-running Tlon monitors during reconnect failures.

## Evidence

### Unit regression (mocked fetch + fake timers)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ ... > openStream > clears the connect timeout when urbitFetch rejects 12ms
 ✓ ... > openStream > clears the connect timeout when the stream response is not ok 10ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

### Production-path connect-timeout storm proof

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.open-stream-timeout.proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ ... > clears connect timers after a real non-OK stream response storm 305ms
 ✓ ... > clears the connect timer when production urbitFetch rejects 10ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

The storm case runs production `openStream` → `urbitFetch` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` against a real loopback `node:http` server that returns `503` five times; real timers; each armed `setTimeout(..., 60000)` is cleared. The reject case uses a closed loopback port (`127.0.0.1:9`) so the production transport fails before headers.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Failed SSE connect attempts no longer leave uncleared 60s AbortController timers, including under repeated failure.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Tlon monitor reconnect → `UrbitSSEClient.openStream` → production `urbitFetch` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → reject or non-OK → `finally { clearTimeout(timeoutId) }`.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime HTTP; loopback `node:http` + closed-port TCP failure; production SSRF-guarded transport (no `urbitFetch` mock, no fake timers).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Same `try/finally { clearTimeout }` pattern as `extensions/zalouser/src/probe.ts`; no new config/API.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with real HTTP listeners and real timers.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.open-stream-timeout.proof.test.ts extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.test.ts --reporter=verbose`

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(restart): keep deferring when pending inspection fails
target.body:
Fixes #104064.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway restart deferral treated pending-work inspection exceptions as proof that the gateway was idle. That fail-open path could restart while active work still existed but could not be inspected. The first patch fixed the helper retry behavior, but the config-reload caller still cleared its restartPending guard from onCheckError even though the helper now keeps polling. A later config change could therefore start duplicate deferral loops and competing restart preparation.

## Summary

- Treat pending-count inspection exceptions as unknown pending work instead of safe-to-restart.
- Keep the existing deferral lifecycle active after both initial and later getPendingCount failures.
- Preserve the config-reload restartPending guard when retrying inspection failures.
- Update the production warning to say the deferral is waiting and retrying instead of restarting immediately.
- Continue polling until a later check confirms idle, or until the explicit maxWaitMs timeout forces the existing timeout path.

## Evidence

Exact-head validation on 422023a5d715b3833c1683df674ae6b57662e4a7:

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/restart.deferral-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts -> passed; 2 shards, 107 tests.
- node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.non-agents.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-non-agents.tsbuildinfo -> passed.
- ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/restart.ts src/infra/restart.deferral-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts -> passed.
- ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/infra/restart.ts src/infra/restart.deferral-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts -> passed.
- pnpm check:loc --base upstream/main --head HEAD -> passed.
- git diff --check -> passed.

Focused behavior covered:

- Initial pending inspection throw calls onCheckError, enters deferral with pending=1, and later emits only after a successful idle check.
- Later polling throw calls onCheckError, keeps polling, and later emits only after a successful idle check.
- Config-reload caller keeps restartPending active after an inspection error; a later config restart request does not create duplicate restart emission work.

## Root Cause

The helper and its production caller disagreed about onCheckError semantics. The helper now treats inspection failure as non-terminal, so the caller must keep its deferral guard active until ready, timeout, cancel, or emission settlement.

## Behavior After This Patch

- Initial inspection throw: calls onCheckError, enters deferral with pending=1, and polls again.
- Later polling throw: calls onCheckError, keeps the interval registered, and retries on the next poll.
- Config reload inspection throw: keeps restartPending true and logs waiting/retrying.
- Confirmed pending=0 still emits restart through the normal ready path.
- Explicit maxWaitMs still preserves the existing forced-timeout behavior.

target.title: fix(gateway): scope accumulatedText preservation to media-only replace events
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multimodal agent users on the OpenResponses gateway would see their assistant reply silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emitted a media-only SSE replace event (`replace: true`, `text: ""`) during streaming.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old guard `typeof text === "string"` treated empty string as valid content, unconditionally resetting `accumulatedText` on any `replace: true` event. The fix scopes accumulated-text preservation to media-bearing replacement events by checking for non-empty `mediaUrls`/`mediaUrl` — the same media-content signal used by the existing SSE coalesce path (`server-chat.ts:1101`). Non-media empty-text replacement continues to clear the buffer per existing behavior.

## User Impact

Users of multimodal agents (image+text input) on the OpenResponses gateway no longer see their assistant replies silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emits a media-only replace event during streaming.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested**: Ubuntu 24.04, Node 22.22.3 (SQLite 3.51.3), branch `fix/bug-001-accumulatedText-empty-replace`
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts
  ```

- **Evidence after fix**:

  ```
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  35 passed (35)
  ```

  Focused regression tests:
  ```
  ✓ preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
  ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrls:[]
  ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrl:""
  ```

- **Shared code alignment.** The agent runtime producer (`agent-runner-execution.ts:2604`) already guards `replace: true` with a truthy `snapshotText` check. The runtime path at `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:1450` produces the exact `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...] }` + `replace: true` event shape that this fix targets.

- **Observed result after fix**: Media-bearing empty-text replacement preserves accumulated assistant text ("Lime green apple") instead of clearing it to "No response from OpenClaw."
- **What was not tested**: Non-streaming paths (not affected — `accumulatedText` is streaming-only). Real multimodal provider E2E flow (the event shape is produced by the agent runtime, not the provider directly; the mock test exercises the exact runtime event sequence).

### Real behavior proof

The fix was verified with a guard condition proof simulating 6 event shapes:

```
Event shape                                | main (bug)      | PR (fixed)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Empty text + valid mediaUrls             | REPLACE (bug!)  | PRESERVE ✓
Empty text + mediaUrls:[]                | REPLACE         | REPLACE ✓
Empty text + mediaUrl:''                 | REPLACE         | REPLACE ✓
Non-empty text (normal replacement)      | REPLACE         | REPLACE ✓
```

The guard condition:
```
main guard:  replace && typeof text === "string"
           = true → accumulatedText = "" ✗ BUG

PR guard:   replace && typeof text === "string" && (text || !hasMediaContent)
           = true && ("" || !true) → false → accumulatedText PRESERVED ✓
```

The agent runtime producer code proves that `{ text: "", replace: true, mediaUrls: [...] }` is always a media-only addition, never an intentional text deletion.

### Regression test plan

3 regression tests cover the behavioral surface:
1. Valid `mediaUrls` → text preserved
2. Empty `mediaUrls: []` → text cleared (existing behavior)
3. Empty `mediaUrl: ""` → text cleared (existing behavior)

All 35 gateway tests pass with zero regression.

target.title: feat(ui): redesign Channels page with guided channel setup wizard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Settings → Channels page was a wall of raw schema-driven config forms — every channel rendered every field (tokens, allowlists, JSON blobs) inline, with no guidance on how to actually connect a channel. A beginner landing on the page had no path from "I want OpenClaw on Telegram" to a working bot: the real setup knowledge (BotFather, Slack manifests, WhatsApp QR pairing) only existed in the CLI wizard (`openclaw channels add`) and the docs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rebuilds Channels in the unified settings design language (#106470) and adds a guided, step-by-step setup wizard to the web UI — without duplicating any setup logic:

- **Gateway (additive protocol):** `wizard.start` gains `flow: "channels"` + `channel` params, routing to the shared channel-setup flow (`openclaw channels add`) over the existing `WizardSession` step protocol already used by the macOS/Android onboarding clients. The wizard branch of `channelsAddCommand` is extracted into a prompter-injectable runner (`src/commands/channels/add-wizard.ts`); the gateway entry never calls `runtime.exit`. On completion the runner reports the channels it actually configured, surfaced as an additive `channels` field on the terminal `wizard.next` result so the client keys channel-specific completion off the real outcome, not the preselection.
- **`SetupChannelsOptions.deferDeviceLinkToClient`:** gateway clients render device linking natively, so the WhatsApp finalize surface skips its terminal QR login; the Control UI runs QR pairing through the existing `web.login.start/wait` RPCs instead.
- **Control UI:** the page becomes "Your channels" (settings-language rows with 44px art tiles and dot statuses: Running / Configured / Needs attention) + "Add a channel" (guided-setup rows incl. a browse-all entry that reaches npm-installable catalog channels), following the unified settings design language (uppercase section headings, one flat group surface, hairline rows, status dots). A detail overlay keeps the full advanced surface: the migrated per-channel settings sections with live status facts, start/relink/logout actions, and the complete schema config form. The wizard modal renders the generic step vocabulary (select / multiselect / text-with-masking / confirm / note with copy button) plus per-channel helper links (BotFather, Discord developer portal, api.slack.com/apps, docs.openclaw.ai) and finishes WhatsApp setup with an embedded QR pairing phase.
- Config writes from the wizard hot-reload channels via the existing chokidar config watcher; no restart needed.

Row/cover art reuses the bundled `plugin-art` set (CSP is `img-src 'self'`, so remote brand icons can't load). The mock-dev harness gains channels/wizard fixtures so the flow is demoable and screenshot-testable offline.

## User Impact

Setting up a channel is now: open Channels → click a card → follow 2–4 short steps → done (WhatsApp ends with a scannable QR right in the dialog). All ~20 channels with setup surfaces work through the same wizard automatically, and everything that was on the old page (full config form, status detail, health JSON) is still there behind the card detail view. CLI behavior is unchanged; the macOS/Android wizard clients are unaffected (protocol change is additive).

target.title: fix(config): warn when JSON5 comments are lost on config write
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw parses `openclaw.json` using JSON5, which supports comments. However, when the configuration is modified, the system saves back using standard `JSON.stringify()`, which strips all user-authored comments.

**Issue**: #105683

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is in `src/config/io.ts` where config writes use `JSON.stringify()` which cannot preserve JSON5 comments.

This PR implements a warning to notify users when their comments will be lost. The warning is **not** gated on `skipOutputLogs` — comment stripping is a data-loss event that should always be surfaced, even for machine-parseable (`--json`) callers.

## User Impact

### Before
- Users add comments to `openclaw.json` for documentation
- Any config modification silently strips all comments

### After  
- Users receive a clear warning when writing config with JSON5 comments
- The warning fires regardless of output mode (including `--json` / `skipOutputLogs`)
- The warning intelligently excludes false positives (URLs in strings)
