target.title: feat(durable): hand off wakes to session queue
target.body:
# PR5/5 - internal session delivery handoff + final hardening

## What Problem This Solves

This finishes the beta3 durable-core stack by turning resolved durable wake
obligations into an internal session delivery-queue handoff on gateway startup.
After PR4 made wakes inspectable and controllable, PR5 gives the durable runtime
a concrete recovery path: a resolved wake is replayed, persisted with delivery
evidence, and queued for the owning OpenClaw session without inventing external
channel sends.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR5/5
- Clean PR5 comparison: `a30e2b6ce4e5f1390599380aedc82078c98854f7..443ffd2292e146fad3c089a03382a5f4702632f7`
- PR4 dependency: `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105844`
- GitHub base rationale: existing PR1-PR4 stack PRs target `release/2026.7.1`; the PR4 branch exists on the fork, not as an upstream base branch, so this PR follows stack convention while documenting the exact PR4-head diff.

## Scope

- Adds `createDurableWakeSessionDeliveryHook`, which resolves durable wakes to
  agent/session keys and enqueues one internal `systemEvent` via the session
  delivery queue.
- Wires gateway startup durable wake replay through that hook.
- Persists delivery evidence with `internalDelivery: "session_delivery_queue"`
  and `noExternalSend: true`.
- Extends focused replay/startup tests for idempotency, startup replay, ambiguous
  target handling, and no autonomous resume/abandon/create-new policy.
- Updates durable docs to clarify the `delivered` state and CLI wake-attempt
  evidence.

## Non-scope

- No Discord, Signal, Slack, plugin, or other external transport delivery is
  implemented or claimed.
- No cron mutation.
- No release/changelog/package churn from the stale old PR5 ancestry.
- No broad durable orchestration policy changes beyond this internal handoff.

## Evidence

Clean scope:

```text
6 files changed, 372 insertions(+), 50 deletions(-)
```

Focused behavior:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/durable/wake-delivery-replay.test.ts src/durable/startup.test.ts
# pass: 2 files, 14 tests
```

Adjacent durable CLI/Gateway/read-path proof:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/durable.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/durable.test.ts src/durable/wake-controls-inspection.test.ts
# pass: 3 Vitest shards, 4 files, 25 tests
```

Static/docs gates:

```bash
pnpm check:test-types
# pass

pnpm check:docs
# pass

git diff --check a30e2b6ce4e5f1390599380aedc82078c98854f7..HEAD
# pass
```

Remote proof attempts were made but unavailable in this shell:

```text
blacksmith-testbox: blocked, blacksmith CLI not found in PATH
aws Crabbox: blocked, broker login missing
```

## Upgrade contract

This PR adds no schema migration. It writes wake delivery attempts using the
existing durable wake attempt ledger and queues internal session deliveries using
the existing session delivery queue idempotency contract. Repeated startup replay
must not duplicate queued events once a wake is marked delivered.

## Risk / limits

- Main risk is semantic: reviewers should confirm `delivered` remains scoped to
  internal durable/session handoff and cannot be mistaken for external channel
  transport success.
- Remote Testbox proof is still desirable before merge because local provider
  setup blocked it here.
- Full release validation was not run for this narrow PR5 slice.

target.title: fix(memory-core): dreaming narrative subagent receives full generic prompt instead of minimal
target.body:
Fixes #105513

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with dreaming enabled would receive bloated system prompts containing 200+ lines of irrelevant tool/channel/exec instructions in dreaming narrative subagent sessions, wasting tokens and degrading dream quality — especially on smaller LLM models.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dreaming narrative subagent session key (`dreaming-narrative-<phase>-<hash>`) does not contain the `subagent:` prefix required by `isSubagentSessionKey()`, so `resolvePromptModeForSession()` returned `"full"` instead of `"minimal"`. The `NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` was appended at the end but drowned out by all the generic instructions.

The fix adds `promptMode` support to the plugin `SubagentRunParams` type and gateway dispatch path, then passes `promptMode: "minimal"` from the dreaming narrative spawn call. This is the correct owner-boundary fix: the plugin explicitly declares its prompt needs instead of relying on session-key convention matching.

## User Impact

Users with dreaming enabled will see significantly smaller system prompts in narrative subagent sessions, reducing token waste and improving dream quality. The `NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` is now the primary context rather than being buried under generic chat instructions. No behavior change for other subagent or session types.

## Evidence

### Before fix
Dreaming narrative session resolved `promptMode` to `"full"` because `dreaming-narrative-*` session keys don't match `isSubagentSessionKey()`:

```
// src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.prompt-helpers.ts:234-239
export function resolvePromptModeForSession(sessionKey?: string): "minimal" | "full" {
  if (!sessionKey) { return "full"; }
  return isSubagentSessionKey(sessionKey) || isCronSessionKey(sessionKey) ? "minimal" : "full";
}
// dreaming-narrative-deep-a1b2c3d4e5f6 → isSubagentSessionKey = false → "full"
```

This caused the full generic prompt with tool summaries (`sessions_spawn`, `image`, exec approval guidance, skill scanning, channel instructions) to be injected into every dream narrative call.

### After fix
The plugin now explicitly passes `promptMode: "minimal"` through the subagent run API:

```ts
// extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-narrative.ts
const run = await params.subagent.run({
  ...
  extraSystemPrompt: NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
  promptMode: "minimal",  // ← new: suppress generic prompt sections
  ...
});
```

In minimal mode, the system prompt builder (`src/agents/system-prompt.ts`) suppresses tool summaries, channel instructions, exec approval guidance, sub-agent delegation, and other irrelevant sections. Only the core identity and the `NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` remain.

**Evidence type**: Code trace and test assertion

**Setup**: OpenClaw main branch (265f79e6072)

Test added in `extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-narrative.test.ts`:
```ts
expect(runOptions.promptMode).toBe("minimal");
```

target.title: fix(gateway): prune channel SecretRef surfaces before eager preflight while crash-loop breaker is tripped
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The persisted Gateway crash-loop breaker claims to enter a control-plane-safe mode that suppresses channel/provider account auto-start, but `prepareGatewayStartupConfig()` performs eager SecretRef preflight **before** the suppression reaches the channel manager. An unavailable channel credential continues to terminate the entire Gateway, and the supervisor keeps restarting it — defeating the safe-mode contract.

Root cause: `pruneSkippedStartupSecretSurfaces()` in `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts` only checks `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS` / `OPENCLAW_SKIP_PROVIDERS` env vars, ignoring the crash-loop breaker's `channelAutostartSuppression`. The breaker computes the suppression in `run.ts:beginBoot()` before calling `startGatewayServer()`, but the secrets activator and `prepareGatewayStartupConfig()` resolve SecretRefs without knowing about it. In one observed incident, 61 identical startup failures occurred over ~15 minutes.

Fixes #106379

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix carries the already-computed `channelAutostartSuppression` into the secrets activator and `prepareGatewayStartupConfig()`, so `pruneSkippedStartupSecretSurfaces()` prunes channel surfaces when the breaker is tripped — just as it already does for the env-var skip paths. This is the narrowest fix: it acts at the earliest point (secrets preflight), leaves the in-process restart/recovery path untouched, and does not mutate `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS` globally.

Alternatives considered and rejected:
- Reordering `channelManager.setAutostartSuppression()` before `prepareGatewayStartupConfig()` — would require creating the channel manager earlier, introducing dependency-on-init ordering risks.
- Mapping the SecretRef error to exit code 78 — treats the symptom, not the root cause; safe mode is meant to keep the control plane available, not just stop restarting.

## User Impact

- **Affected**: supervised Gateways (systemd, launchd) with an unavailable SecretRef on an enabled channel, where the persisted crash-loop breaker has tripped.
- **Before**: the Gateway process keeps exiting with status 1, the supervisor restarts it, and the control plane remains unreachable.
- **After**: when the breaker trips, channel surfaces are pruned before SecretRef resolution, the Gateway starts successfully with channel auto-start suppressed, and operators can access the control plane (Web UI, API) to diagnose and repair.
- Normal (non-tripped) startup behavior is unchanged. Gateway auth and non-channel required secrets remain fail-closed.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-startup-config.secrets.test.ts` — 52 passed (2 test files, 2 shards). 4 new test cases:
  - breaker suppression active → channel surfaces pruned before SecretRef resolution
  - breaker suppression null → channels preserved (regression guard for normal startup)
  - breaker active + gateway auth SecretRef → gateway auth still resolves, channels pruned
  - `prepareGatewayStartupConfig` integration → channels pruned end-to-end
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts src/gateway/server.impl.ts src/gateway/server-startup-config.secrets.test.ts` — clean
- `pnpm format:check` — clean
- Review: passed (best fix, no P0/P1/P2 findings)

Behavior addressed: crash-loop breaker safe mode — after the breaker is tripped, channel SecretRefs are pruned from startup secret preflight so the control plane starts.

Real environment tested: unit test suite covering both `createRuntimeSecretsActivator` and `prepareGatewayStartupConfig` paths with breaker suppression active/null.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```
pnpm test src/gateway/server-startup-config.secrets.test.ts
```

Evidence after fix: all 52 tests pass (2 shards), including 4 new breaker-suppression tests that verify channel surfaces are pruned from SecretRef preflight when the breaker is tripped, channels remain when it is not, and gateway auth continues to resolve.

Observed result after fix: `pruneSkippedStartupSecretSurfaces(config, channelAutostartSuppression)` returns `config` with `channels: undefined` when breaker suppression is active, preventing the unavailable channel credential from blocking startup. The suppression is carried from `run.ts:beginBoot()` → `startGatewayServer()` → `createRuntimeSecretsActivator()` / `prepareGatewayStartupConfig()` → secrets preflight.

What was not tested: full-systemd crash-loop reproduction with real unavailable credentials on a live Linux host. The unit tests exercise the exact code paths (fast-path secrets preflight, full secrets runtime, `prepareGatewayStartupConfig` integration) with mocked breaker state, which provides deterministic coverage of the ordering fix.

Fixes an issue where a slow device-pair notification poll could overlap later 10-second ticks and race notification state or send duplicate pairing reminders.

## Why This Change Was Made

The notifier now keeps one service-lifetime poll in flight and skips interval ticks until it settles. The guard releases after success or failure, while initial polling, delivery behavior, cadence, and stop semantics remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Users no longer receive duplicate pairing notifications because one slow delivery crossed a polling interval, and polling resumes normally after the pending work settles.

target.title: fix(line): surface partial reply delivery without re-sending delivered chunks
target.body:
Fixes #106333

## What Problem This Solves

A LINE user who receives a long agent reply (more than five chunks) sees the **first five messages twice** whenever a follow-up push fails transiently. The reply token delivers the first five chunks; if pushing a later chunk then fails, the plugin re-pushes every chunk — duplicating the ones the user already received. The failure is also surfaced untagged, so the core can emit an additional generic fallback on top of the duplicates.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `sendLineReplyChunks`, one `try` wrapped the reply send, the remaining-push loop, and the `return`, so a push failure *after* a successful reply was caught by the same `catch` that handles a genuine reply-token failure and fell through to the "push everything" fallback.

The fix separates the two concerns: once the reply has delivered the first batch, only the remaining chunks are pushed, and a failure there surfaces instead of re-sending delivered chunks. Any error propagated after content already reached the user is tagged so `isVisiblePartialDeliveryError` (`src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts`) recognises it and the core suppresses a duplicate fallback — the same contract the rich/media partial path already uses. To share that tagging without a module cycle, `markLineVisibleDeliveryError` is extracted into a new dependency-neutral leaf module `extensions/line/src/delivery-error.ts`, imported by both `reply-chunks.ts` and `auto-reply-delivery.ts` (no `reply-chunks ↔ auto-reply-delivery` cycle). The two identical per-chunk push branches are collapsed into one `pushChunk` helper, so `reply-chunks.ts` is net shorter.

Independent of the open reliability PRs in this area (e.g. #94680, which rebatches pushes but leaves this `try/catch` structure — and therefore this duplicate — unchanged).

## User Impact

Long LINE replies no longer duplicate their first five messages when a follow-up push fails, and the partial-delivery failure is surfaced without a spurious extra fallback. No behavior change for replies that fit the reply token or that succeed.

## Evidence

### Red / green regression test

New test in `reply-chunks.test.ts`: the reply delivers `one`..`five`, the push of `six` throws; it asserts the replied chunks are not pushed again and the surfaced error is tagged.

On current `main` (bug present):

```
 × does not re-send reply-delivered chunks when a later push fails
AssertionError: expected [ 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', …(1) ] to not include 'one'
 ❯ extensions/line/src/reply-chunks.test.ts:215:24
    215|     expect(pushed).not.toContain("one");
 Tests  1 failed | 4 passed (5)
```

With this change:

```
 Tests  5 passed (5)
```
### Real LINE chat — before vs after (live account)

Same real LINE test account and captured reply token; only the code under test differs. Five short chunks (`c1`..`c5`) fill the reply batch, chunk 6 is 5001 chars so its push is rejected by LINE with a genuine HTTP 400.

**Before (current `main`) — `c1`..`c5` delivered twice (duplicate):**

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/edenfunf/moltbot/evidence/106336-real-line/106336-before.png)

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
[push]  delivered 1 message  (×5  → c1..c5 re-sent)
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? YES (bug)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: false / visibleReplySent: false
```

**After (this change) — `c1`..`c5` delivered once:**

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/edenfunf/moltbot/evidence/106336-real-line/106336-after.png)

```
pushed (successful) chunks: []
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? NO (fixed)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: true / visibleReplySent: true
```

### End-to-end (real delivery path)

Driving the real `deliverLineAutoReply` → real `sendLineReplyChunks` with the same scenario:

- on `main`: `one`..`five` are re-pushed (duplicates);
- with this change: only the chunk after the failure is pushed, `one`..`five` are never re-pushed, and the thrown error carries `{ sentBeforeError: true, visibleReplySent: true }`.

### Real LINE run (live account + API)

Captured a real reply token from an inbound webhook, then drove the real `sendLineReplyChunks` with the real LINE reply/push API. Five short chunks (`c1`..`c5`) fill the reply batch; chunk 6 is 5001 characters, so its push is rejected by LINE with a genuine **HTTP 400** (recipient/token redacted):

**Before (current `main`)** — the reply delivers `c1`..`c5`, the oversized push 400s, and the fallback re-pushes every chunk, so `c1`..`c5` are delivered **twice**:

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
[push]  delivered 1 message  (×5  → c1..c5 re-sent)
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? YES (bug)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: false / visibleReplySent: false
```

**After (this change)** — the reply delivers `c1`..`c5`, the oversized push 400s, and the delivered chunks are **not** re-sent; the error is tagged:

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
pushed (successful) chunks: []
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? NO (fixed)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: true / visibleReplySent: true
```

In the LINE chat, `c1`..`c5` appear twice before the fix and exactly once after.

### Checks

```
oxfmt --check              → clean (4 files)
oxlint                     → 0 problems
tsgo (extensions)          → no errors in the touched files
check:import-cycles        → 0 runtime value cycles
check:madge-import-cycles  → 0 cycles (reply-chunks ↔ auto-reply-delivery cycle removed)
LINE suite                 → reply-chunks.test.ts + auto-reply-delivery.test.ts: 14 passed
```

target.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle
target.body:
Closes #99054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users who remove a personal app/bot and later add it again can continue the same OpenClaw server-side DM session, allowing the bot to use prior conversation context after an app lifecycle boundary.

This targets Teams app-management lifecycle signals that the bot can actually observe. Live capture showed Teams' local "Remove chat history" action can arrive later as an ordinary message in the same personal `conversation.id`, with no `installationUpdate`, `conversationUpdate`, `membersAdded`, or `membersRemoved` activity. This PR does not claim to detect that fully local clear-chat action when Teams gives the bot no lifecycle or conversation-boundary signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teams now routes `installationUpdate` removal activities and bot `membersRemoved` conversation updates into a lifecycle handler. On a removal boundary, the handler removes the cached Teams conversation reference, rotates the matching OpenClaw session entry to a new session id with `updatedAt: 0`, and clears provider-owned route/delivery/origin metadata so the next inbound message cannot resume the removed chat transcript.

The handler also treats a personal `installationUpdate action=add` as a reinstall boundary only when an existing route-matched Teams DM session is already active. That catches tenants or flows where the re-add signal is visible but the prior remove signal was missed, without resetting first-time installs. Finally, inbound personal DMs check for a stored same-user/same-bot conversation reference with a different Teams `conversation.id`; when Teams exposes that boundary, OpenClaw removes the previous reference and rotates the DM session.

## User Impact

After a true Teams app removal and re-add, the next inbound message starts from a fresh OpenClaw session instead of silently resuming prior DM or channel context. Operators also avoid retaining a cached proactive-send reference for the removed Teams conversation.

For Teams clear-chat/reopen flows, the patch protects the observable case where Teams gives the bot a new personal conversation id. If Teams reuses the same server-side conversation id and sends no lifecycle event, there is no bot-visible signal in the captured payloads; that remains a Teams platform limitation rather than a claim made by this PR.

Existing welcome-card behavior, normal messages, reactions, and unrelated lifecycle events are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live corrected Dale smoke:
  - Baseline before app removal used a synthetic marker.
  - Teams app removal emitted `installationUpdate action=remove`.
  - Handler logged `msteams lifecycle remove handled`, `reason=installation-remove`, `conversationType=personal`, `conversationRemoved=true`, `sessionsReset=1`.
  - The session entry rotated to a new redacted session id with `updatedAt: 0` and no Teams route/delivery/origin metadata.
  - After re-add, Teams showed the welcome card and the verification prompt used a fresh session; the bot did not recall the pre-removal marker.
- Live Teams `Remove chat history` follow-up after deploying this branch:
  - Sent a synthetic pre-clear marker.
  - Used Teams `Remove chat history`, opened the app/chat again, and sent a verification prompt.
  - No `installationUpdate add`, lifecycle/remove activity, or DM conversation-boundary handler log appeared.
  - The same OpenClaw session id remained active, and the bot could recall the pre-clear marker.
  - This confirms the PR should not claim to fix Teams local clear-history behavior when Teams sends no lifecycle event and reuses the same server-side conversation id.
- Added regression coverage for:
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove`
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove-upgrade`
  - first-install `installationUpdate/add` with no active session
  - personal `installationUpdate/add` when an existing session is active
  - ignored channel `installationUpdate/add`
  - channel bot `membersRemoved`
  - ignored non-bot `membersRemoved`
  - race-safe session rotation
  - personal DM conversation-id boundary rotation
  - no rotation for matching personal conversation ids
  - no rotation for different stored bot ids
- Added monitor-level coverage proving the Teams activity shim dispatches `installationUpdate` and `membersRemoved` activities to registered lifecycle handlers.
- Validation:
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts` - 11 tests passed.

target.title: fix(reply): use document cap for local media attachments
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refs #40880 for the Telegram outbound reply-media path.

Telegram can send generated local documents larger than 5 MiB, but final-reply media staging was dropping an unconfigured 23,456,667 byte PPTX before it reached Telegram `sendDocument`. Direct Telegram `sendDocument` for the same file succeeded, so the failing boundary was local reply-media staging rather than the Telegram adapter or the PPTX MIME type.

## Summary

Local final-reply attachments sent back to Telegram now use the document media cap when no explicit `mediaMaxMb` is configured.

## Change

- Preserve explicit channel/account/default `mediaMaxMb` overrides.
- Use the 100 MiB document cap only for unconfigured Telegram reply-media staging.
- Keep unconfigured non-Telegram reply-media staging on the existing 5 MiB media-store cap.
- Add focused tests for the Telegram default cap and the non-Telegram fallback.

## Evidence

Real failure observed on a Telegram reply with:

- `MEDIA:./tmp/izen_shooting/Annual_CIS_Conference_2026_RU.pptx`
- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation`
- `23,456,667` bytes

Focused validation after this patch:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/reply-media-paths.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.final-media-runreplyagent.test.ts
# 2 files passed, 26 tests passed
```

Live Telegram smoke proof from a real OpenClaw Telegram reply:

![Redacted Telegram screenshot showing an 8.0 MB PPTX delivered without Media failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/pr-99189-proof-assets/proofs/pr-99189/telegram-pptx-8mb-proof-redacted.jpg)

- File shown by Telegram: `test_local_reply_media_8mb_...pptx`
- Telegram UI size/type: `8.0 MB PPTX`
- Result: the document is visible in Telegram without `Media failed`

Telegram limit note: the cloud Bot API upload limit is 50 MB for documents, while a self-hosted local Bot API server supports uploads up to 2000 MB. This proof intentionally stays inside the normal cloud `sendDocument` envelope while crossing the old 5 MiB reply-media staging cap.

## Summary

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's agent-testing guidance hardcoded Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. That caused agents to override an existing explicit Crabbox choice such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`, even though the wrapper already supports that environment override before the repository's Blacksmith default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The testing and Crabbox skills now tell trusted agent workflows to omit `--provider` unless a specific proof or safety route requires one. This preserves the existing wrapper selection contract:

1. an explicitly requested/command-line provider;
2. platform routing such as automatic Azure selection for Windows/WSL2;
3. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
4. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills distinguish the configured environment/repository provider reported by `crabbox config show --json` from the actual backend selected for a command. The wrapper's emitted `[crabbox] ... provider=...` diagnostic is authoritative for actual provider attribution, including explicit overrides and automatic platform routing.

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and avoid inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. The PR was narrowed accordingly: it does not change `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs`, adds no merged-config precedence contract, and adds no new fail-closed startup behavior.

AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

## User Impact

Developers who explicitly set `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` can run ordinary trusted agent validation on that backend without agents forcing Blacksmith Testbox. Developers without an explicit override continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default.

A configured local container still executes tests inside a Crabbox-managed Docker lease; it does not silently downgrade to host-local execution. Remote, cross-platform, untrusted-source, and Testbox-specific proof requirements continue to select their required backend explicitly.

## Evidence

- Blind `acpx claude` validation independently resolved the inherited `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`; the prompt did not name the expected provider.
- The first agent attempt exposed a guidance defect by running the focused test directly on the host. That result was rejected, and the skills were clarified to require wrapper-managed Docker execution for `local-container`.
- Post-fix Claude runs correctly provisioned local-container Docker leases, ran the focused wrapper suite inside the containers, and cleaned up their leases.
- Provider-attribution probe: configured provider `local-container`; wrapper invoked with explicit `--provider aws` emitted `provider=aws`, confirming why wrapper output must be authoritative.
- Final post-rebase proof:
  - base: `upstream/main` at `161525d43c4c0157a8fd4feceb2bf96cb4db5900`;
  - provider/runtime: `provider=local-container`, `runtime=docker`, Crabbox `0.37.1`;
  - lease: `cbx_29a3dd41d47d` / `brisk-crab-d2c5`, explicitly deleted after the run;
  - command: `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --id cbx_29a3dd41d47d --timing-json -- corepack pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts --reporter=default`;
  - result: 1 test file passed; 192/192 tests passed.
- Final diff relative to `upstream/main`: two skill files only; zero wrapper/test code diff.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output` on `e0bb1c889ae` changes — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
